task: Use the Cambridge Dictionary to understand the rules for forming and using comparative and superlative adjectives in English Grammar, including example sentences.
answer: Used the Cambridge Dictionary Grammar section to understand comparative and superlative adjective rules. Navigated from the homepage to the Grammar area, then to the article 'Comparison: adjectives (bigger, biggest, more interesting)' at https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/comparison-adjectives-bigger-biggest-more-interesting. Key rules extracted: (1) Comparative adjectives compare one person/thing with another ('than' is used); (2) Superlative adjectives describe one person/thing as having more of a quality than all others; (3) One-syllable adjectives take -er (comparative) and -est (superlative) suffixes; (4) 'the' is normally used before a superlative adjective; (5) Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y change y to i and take -ier/-iest; (6) Adjectives with three or more syllables use more/less (comparative) and most/least (superlative); (7) Some one-syllable adjectives are irregular (good/better/best, bad/worse/worst, far/farther-further/farthest-furthest); (8) Never combine more/most with -er/-est endings.
